items.text: Under HIFA, the printed portion of a home improvement installment contract must be in type of at least what size?
B. 8-point — MCL 445.1201 requires the contract to be dated, in writing, with the printed portion in at least 8-point type; 10-point bold is reserved for the heading and notices.
The words 'home improvement installment contract' must appear at the top of a HIFA contract or above the buyer's signature line in at least what type style?
D. 10-point bold type — MCL 445.1202 requires the words 'home improvement installment contract' in at least 10-point bold type at the top or above the buyer's signature line.
A contractor signs a HIFA installment contract with a homeowner but never delivers a completed copy to the buyer. What is the legal effect?

A. The buyer is not obligated to pay until a completed copy is delivered — MCL 445.1204 requires delivery of a completed copy at the time of execution; until the contractor delivers it, the buyer is not obligated to pay.
A homeowner pays for a $9,000 bathroom remodel using a loan she obtained directly from her own bank. Does HIFA govern the transaction?

C. No - a loan the buyer obtains directly from a bank is excluded from HIFA — MCL 445.1102(l)(v) excludes financing the buyer obtains directly from a bank; HIFA covers credit extended through the contractor.
A builder offers installment financing to a customer for construction of a brand-new home. Does HIFA apply?

B. No - new-home construction is excluded from HIFA — MCL 445.1102(g) and (k) define covered goods and services as modernization, rehabilitation, repair, alteration, or improvement - but not construction of new homes.
Which of the following sales is excluded from HIFA even when financed on installments?
A. A free-standing refrigerator — MCL 445.1102(l) excludes free-standing appliances such as a stove, freezer, refrigerator, non-central air conditioner, and water heater from HIFA.
What is the maximum penalty for a first-offense willful violation of HIFA?
D. Misdemeanor - up to 90 days and/or a $500 fine — MCL 445.1421 makes a willful HIFA violation a misdemeanor punishable by up to 90 days and/or a $500 fine for a first offense.
A HIFA installment contract contains a clause in which the buyer waives all claims and defenses against the contractor's assignee. What is the effect?

C. The clause is void, but the rest of the contract stands — MCL 445.1206 prohibits a buyer's waiver of claims or defenses against the contractor or assignee; the offending provision is void while the remainder of the contract stands.
A contractor is convicted of a second willful HIFA violation. What is the maximum jail term?
B. 1 year — MCL 445.1421 raises the maximum for a subsequent willful violation to up to 1 year; 90 days applies only to a first offense.
A contractor finances a home improvement with a cash price of exactly $300 through an installment contract. Is the transaction covered by HIFA?

D. No - HIFA requires a cash price in excess of $300, so exactly $300 is excluded — MCL 445.1102 requires a cash price in excess of $300; a price of exactly $300 or less is excluded, and $600 is the separate licensure-exemption figure in MCL 339.2403.
An exam prep book states that 'MCL 445.1108 requires a written contract for all home improvements over $600.' What is wrong with that statement?

A. MCL 445.1108 does not exist, and HIFA has no general $600 written-contract rule — The corpus verifies that MCL 445.1108 does not exist and there is no general HIFA $600 written-contract rule; HIFA's trigger is a cash price over $300 on installment credit.
A homeowner mails her HSSA cancellation notice by regular mail, properly addressed with postage prepaid, on the third business day. When is the cancellation effective?
C. When it is deposited in the mail — MCL 445.112(3) makes a mailed HSSA cancellation effective when deposited in the mail, properly addressed with postage prepaid.
One day after signing a home solicitation sale, the seller sends a courier to the buyer's home to collect the down payment. Is this permitted?

D. No - the seller may not have payment picked up at the residence before the 3-business-day period expires — MCL 445.112(1) bars the seller from having a courier or third party pick up payment at the residence before the 3-business-day cancellation period expires.
A buyer cancels an HSSA sale and makes the delivered materials available at her residence. The seller never picks them up. After how many days may she keep or dispose of the goods?
B. 20 days — MCL 445.113(2) lets the buyer keep or dispose of the goods if the seller does not pick them up within 20 days of cancellation.
Besides the cancellation statement near the signature line, what must an HSSA contract physically include?

A. A duplicate notice-of-cancellation form attached or printed on the reverse — MCL 445.113(1)-(2) requires the cancellation statement near the signature line plus a duplicate notice of cancellation form attached to the contract or printed on its reverse.
Which right must the HIFA 'Notice to buyer' disclose?

C. The right to prepay the balance in full with a partial refund of the finance charge — MCL 445.1202 requires the Notice to buyer to state, among other things, the right to pay off the balance in advance with a partial refund of the finance charge, along with the rescission right and the right to a filled-in copy.
Under the Construction Lien Act, the required statement that contractors must be licensed may be printed in type no smaller than what?
B. The type size of the contract body — MCL 570.1114 requires the licensure statement in type no smaller than the body of the contract itself.
Mid-project, a homeowner verbally asks a licensed builder to add a $8,000 deck, and the builder proceeds on a handshake. What is the lien consequence?

D. Lien rights for the added work are at risk - amendments and additions must also be in writing — MCL 570.1114 conditions residential lien rights on the written contract AND written amendments or additions; a verbal change order puts lien rights at risk.
An unlicensed handyman performs a $500 residential repair, labor and materials combined. Which statement is true?

C. The work is exempt from builder licensure because it is under $600 — MCL 339.2403 exempts work under $600 (labor plus materials combined) from residential builder licensure; it is a licensure exemption only, not a contract rule.
An unlicensed builder completes a $30,000 residential remodel and the owner refuses to pay. Can the builder sue to collect?

A. No - an unlicensed builder cannot sue to collect compensation for residential work — MCL 339.2412 bars an unlicensed builder from bringing an action to collect compensation for residential work, at any contract amount.
Which of the following is NOT one of the five elements of a valid contract?
D. Notarization — The five elements are offer, acceptance, consideration, capacity, and legality; notarization is not required for a valid contract (corpus Domain 03 section 5).
In a unit-price contract, how is cost risk allocated?

B. Shared - the contractor bears unit-cost risk and the owner bears quantity risk — Under a unit-price contract, risk is shared: the contractor bears the risk of unit cost and the owner bears the risk of quantities (corpus contract-types table).
Under a time-and-materials contract, which party bears the risk of cost overruns?
A. The owner — Under time and materials, like cost-plus, the owner bears the cost risk; fixed-price puts the risk on the contractor (corpus contract-types table).
A remodel reaches the point where the owner can use the space for its intended purpose, but punch-list items remain. What has occurred?

C. Substantial completion - triggering retainage release and warranty start — Substantial completion means the owner can use the work for its intended purpose and triggers retainage release and warranty start; final completion requires the punch list and all obligations done (corpus 03 §5).
An owner materially breaches, forcing the contractor off the job. Before claiming damages, what duty does the contractor owe?
B. A duty to mitigate damages — The non-breaching party has a duty to mitigate damages; material breach excuses further performance but not the mitigation duty (corpus 03 §5, breach and remedies).
A tornado shuts down a jobsite for three weeks. Under a typical force majeure clause, what relief does the contractor get?

D. An extension of time - but not an increase in price — Force majeure excuses or extends performance for events beyond the parties' control; it extends time but does not raise the price (corpus 03 §5).
What is the statute of limitations for a negligence claim involving injury to person or property in Michigan?
A. 3 years from the death or injury — MCL 600.5805(2) sets a 3-year limitations period for negligence claims running from the death or injury; 6 years is the contract period under MCL 600.5807(9).
A homeowner proves GROSS negligence against a builder for a defect discovered 8 years after occupancy. Under the statute of repose, when must suit be filed?

C. Within 1 year after discovery, subject to an absolute 10-year cap from occupancy — MCL 600.5839(1)(b) gives gross-negligence claimants 1 year after discovery to sue, with an absolute cap of 10 years from occupancy, use, or acceptance.
A builder gave a 1-year express warranty that has expired. In year 3, the homeowner sues over sloppy framing. Which is correct?

D. The implied warranty of workmanship exists independently and may still support the claim — The implied warranty of workmanship exists independently of express warranties - an expired 1-year express warranty does not extinguish it, though repose still caps claims at 6 years from occupancy (corpus 03 §7).
A contractor's employee drops a tool and injures a passerby. Separately, the contractor's own finished deck fails. Which loss does the contractor's CGL policy cover?
A. The injury to the passerby, but not the contractor's own defective work product — CGL covers third-party bodily injury and property damage but not the contractor's own work product (corpus 03 §8).
